constraints: The netlist must be plain-text structural Verilog using standard cell primitives or simple DFF/AND/OR/INV models simulatable with iverilog, with no proprietary cell libraries.

The design brief must describe the module's intended functional behavior and state that a global synchronous reset RSTN is expected to clear all state-holding registers to their defined reset values, without mentioning any known defect.
All flip-flop instance names in the netlist must be unique and follow a consistent naming pattern (e.g. u_*_ff*) so instance-name matching in the report is unambiguous.

The provided testbench must exercise at least one reset assertion after the design has reached a non-reset operational state, and must dump observable state-flop values before and after the reset pulse so reset-clearing behavior can be checked by simulation.

Post-initialization steady-state functional behavior (outputs under normal non-reset operation) must be identical regardless of any reset-wiring anomaly, so the anomaly is only observable via reset traces, not via functional mismatches during normal operation.

functional_requirements.requirement: trojan_report.json must be valid JSON containing all four required top-level fields (trojan_present, suspect_flops, anomaly_description, reset_net_summary) with the exact types specified in the interface.

Every string listed in suspect_flops must correspond to an actual flip-flop cell instance name present in gate_netlist.v (verifiable by grepping/parsing the netlist); unknown or misspelled instance names invalidate the entry.
reset_net_summary must account for every state-holding flip-flop instance in gate_netlist.v exactly once across its net groupings (no flop omitted, no flop double-counted).
anomaly_description must be a non-empty string of at least 20 characters when trojan_present is true; it may be an empty string only when trojan_present is false.

interface: The submission is a single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json (no other files are graded; the netlist and testbench under inputs/ must NOT be modified). The file must contain a top-level JSON object with exactly these fields: (1) "trojan_present": boolean, true if any flip-flop's effective reset polarity/path differs from the documented common reset net RSTN feeding the majority of flops. (2) "suspect_flops": array of strings, each the exact Verilog instance name (as it appears in gate_netlist.v) of a flip-flop identified as having anomalous reset wiring; must be empty array if trojan_present is false. (3) "anomaly_description": string, a free-text technical description (minimum 20 characters) of the mechanism causing the anomaly (e.g. inverted reset net, missing reset connection, gated reset). (4) "reset_net_summary": object mapping each distinct reset-driving net or signal name found in the netlist to an array of flip-flop instance names driven by that net/signal. All four fields are required; extra fields are ignored. Instance names must match exactly (case-sensitive) the names used in gate_netlist.v.
objective: Analyze the provided gate-level netlist of a small controller/datapath module and produce a structured report auditing how the synchronous reset signal is distributed to every state-holding flip-flop in the design. Identify any flip-flops whose effective reset behavior deviates from the majority reset behavior documented in the design brief, and list every flip-flop instance together with the reset polarity/logic that actually drives its reset pin as determined by tracing the netlist.
response_format: A single JSON file submission/trojan_report.json matching the schema described in public_spec.interface.
